about: Blaufränkisch is Central Europe’s great cool-climate red, at home in Austria and Hungary, and a natural fit for a winery founded by a Central European. Dr. Konstantin Frank, a Ukrainian-born viticulturist of German descent, began planting European grapes on Keuka Lake in 1958 when almost no one believed they could survive there. His descendants have kept exploring grapes from that part of the world, from Grüner Veltliner to Rkatsiteli and Saperavi, and Blaufränkisch, which Germans call Lemberger, is part of that thread.

The fruit is 100% from the family’s Seneca Lake estate in Hector, planted to Blaufränkisch in 2014 in deep Honeoye silt loam within the warm “Banana Belt.” The winery calls 2020 hot and dry: budbreak came late, in mid-May, but dry weather kept disease away and the grapes ripened fully into October. After destemming and a cold soak, the wine fermented in open-top stainless steel with punchdowns and pumpovers, then aged 18 months in French oak, 20 percent new.

The winery describes fresh plum and red berries with violet scents, moving from a bright, fruity core to spicy richness, with juicy acidity, earthy notes and cedar from the oak. Wine Enthusiast rated the 2020 90 points. Coming from a hot, dry season in which the grapes hung until fully ripe, and now with several years in bottle, it shows how well this Austrian grape has taken to the warmer eastern shore of Seneca Lake.
